rows.name: Gemini Robotics
rows.description: Gemini Robotics 2.5 (Google DeepMind): vision-language-action (VLA) model that can control robots of any shape, from tabletop arms to full humanoids, including whole-body control and 22-DoF dexterous hands. Early access via waitlist.

rows.name: Deepmind Apptronik Apollo
rows.description: MuJoCo model (MJCF) of the Apptronik Apollo humanoid in Google DeepMind's MuJoCo Menagerie collection. Requires MuJoCo 3.0+; released under Apache-2.0.

rows.name: NVIDIA Cosmos
rows.description: NVIDIA Cosmos: open platform of world foundation models, datasets and tools for building physical AI for robots, autonomous vehicles and smart infrastructure.

rows.name: NVIDIA Isaac Sim
rows.description: NVIDIA Isaac Sim: reference application to design, simulate, test and train AI-based robots in physically based virtual environments, including synthetic data generation.

rows.name: NVIDIA OSMO
rows.description: NVIDIA OSMO: cloud-native orchestration platform that schedules multi-stage, multi-container robotics workloads (data generation, training, simulation) across on-premises, private and public clouds.

rows.name: NVIDIA Flora
rows.description: NVIDIA Flora: open model suite and data engine used to train GR00T models; it produces timestamped action instructions, dense process rewards and episode outcome rewards for human and robot manipulation video.

rows.name: NVIDIA Aspire
rows.description: NVIDIA ASPIRE (Agentic Skill Programming through Iterative Robot Exploration): continual-learning system that autonomously discovers reusable robot skills by writing and refining code-as-policy control programs.

rows.name: Lerobot
rows.description: LeRobot (Hugging Face): open-source library for end-to-end robot learning, with models, datasets and tools for data collection, training and deployment on real and simulated robots.

rows.name: ROS
rows.description: ROS (Robot Operating System): open-source SDK of libraries, drivers and tools for building robot applications, supported by Open Robotics; ROS 2 is the current generation used from research to production.

rows.name: T-Robotics
rows.description: Trener Robotics: AI software platform that lets industrial robots operate autonomously, adapt to variability and be deployed faster in manufacturing.

rows.name: Genesis
rows.description: Genesis World (formerly Genesis): open-source simulation platform for physical AI combining a multi-physics engine, photo-realistic renderer and cross-platform compiler behind a Python API. Started as an academic project in Dec 2024, now supported by Genesis AI.

rows.name: GRID
rows.description: General Robotics (scaledfoundations.ai now redirects here): AI company building GRID, a modular 'intelligence grid' that brings adaptable AI to any robot form, task or environment.

rows.name: Skild Brain (Skild AI)
rows.description: Skild AI: company building the Skild Brain, a unified 'omni-bodied' robot foundation model meant to control any robot for any task, applied to inspection, mobile manipulation and packing.

rows.name: Rapyuta
rows.description: Rapyuta Robotics (Japan): warehouse automation company offering the Rapyuta ASRS storage system, pick-assist AMRs and end-to-end software for people-robot collaboration in warehouses.

rows.name: Realtime
rows.description: Realtime Robotics: motion-planning and simulation software to simulate, test and optimize robotic systems in parallel and deploy multi-robot cells faster.

rows.name: Braincorp
rows.description: Brain Corp: autonomous technology company that provides AI software and autonomy for commercial robots, aimed at more productive operations.

rows.name: Field AI
rows.description: FieldAI: embodied AI software ('One Autonomy for All Robots') that gives mobile robots autonomy in unstructured real-world environments, independent of the robot platform.

rows.name: Asimovo
rows.description: Asimovo (Rotterdam, founded 2023): cloud 'RoboDevOps' platform where teams simulate, develop and test robots and their AI in one browser workspace with ROS, Gazebo and asset libraries.

rows.name: Intrinsic (Google)
rows.description: Intrinsic: Alphabet software and AI robotics company building a platform for intelligent industrial automation.

rows.name: Open Duck
rows.description: Open Duck Mini: open-source project to build a ~35 cm miniature of Disney's BDX droid, with CAD, BOM and walking policies trained in Isaac Gym (AWD) and transferred to the real robot.

rows.name: Reachy Pollen Robotics
rows.description: Official Pollen Robotics Docker image with a standalone Reachy 2 core, for demos, testing and development without the physical robot.

rows.name: Robot Simulators
rows.description: Best-of-robot-simulators: curated GitHub list ranking open-source robot simulators, regenerated weekly.

rows.name: Open Loong
rows.description: OpenLoong hardware repository: open-source hardware documentation (drawings, designs, specs and perception system) of the QingLoong full-size humanoid robot.

rows.name: PyRoki
rows.description: PyRoki: modular, extensible, cross-platform Python toolkit for robot kinematic optimization.
other_descriptions: A modular, extensible, and cross-platform toolkit for kinematic optimization.

rows.name: Encord
rows.description: Encord: multimodal data platform for physical AI to manage, curate, annotate and align large datasets, from sensor streams to video and text.

rows.name: Robobrain
rows.description: RoboBrain (BAAI): embodied AI foundation model family; RoboBrain 2.5 adds depth-aware 3D spatial reasoning, manipulation trace prediction and dense temporal progress estimation.

rows.name: Genesis AI
rows.description: Genesis AI: physical AI company that supports the Genesis World simulator and is developing the Eno robot, with targeted customer deployments planned by end of 2026.

rows.name: General Bionix
rows.description: General Bionix: no-code, vision-based AI platform that lets factory operators program robotic arms from a single human demonstration; hardware agnostic, focused on high-mix manufacturing.

rows.name: AUIbot
rows.description: UAIbot: multi-language, web-based 3D robotics simulator for interactive robotics learning and research.

rows.name: Reachy2-UnityDigitalTwin
rows.description: Pollen Robotics Unity package that mirrors the state of a real or simulated Reachy 2 robot as a digital twin.

rows.name: OpenMind
rows.description: OpenMind: deployment layer for agentic robotics; runs robot fleets on Arc, its suite of models for mapping, navigation, dexterity and human-robot interaction.

rows.name: Newton
rows.description: Newton: open-source, GPU-accelerated physics simulation engine built on NVIDIA Warp, aimed at roboticists and simulation researchers.

rows.name: Lightwheel
rows.description: Lightwheel: provides SimReady 3D assets, synthetic and egocentric human data, and evaluation platforms for embodied AI and robot learning.

rows.name: Deliverance
rows.description: Deliverance Enterprises (Valencia/Castellón, Spain): service robotics integrator offering cleaning and waiter robots, IoT and a fleet management platform for hospitality, healthcare and industry.

rows.name: Cosmicbrain
rows.description: CosmicBrain: supervised humanoid robot deployments for data center operations (rack inspection rounds, parts logistics) with defined operating limits and measured task performance.

rows.name: Build
rows.description: Build AI: vertically integrated 'data hyperscaler' for physical AI that collects large egocentric datasets of real human labor (Egocentric-10K, Egocentric-100K) for robot model training.

rows.name: Foxglove
rows.description: Foxglove: data platform for robotics to collect, visualize, search and debug fleet data and curate datasets for model training.

rows.name: Generalist
rows.description: Generalist AI: company building embodied foundation models (GEN-1, GEN-1.5) for general-purpose robot manipulation, trained on large-scale physical experience.

rows.name: UMI
rows.description: UMI (Universal Manipulation Interface): data collection and policy learning framework using hand-held grippers to transfer in-the-wild human demonstrations directly into deployable robot policies.

rows.name: GentleHumanoid
rows.description: GentleHumanoid: research paper (arXiv 2511.04679) on learning upper-body compliance for humanoids, enabling safe contact-rich interaction with humans and objects via RL.

rows.name: Flexion
rows.description: Flexion: unified robot foundation model combining command, motion and control, trained in simulation with reinforcement learning and deployable on humanoids, wheeled platforms and arms.

rows.name: Neuracore
rows.description: Neuracore: robot learning platform and open-source library (MIT) for streaming data logging, dataset visualization, cloud training and real-time policy deployment.

rows.name: Scanford
rows.description: Scanford (Stanford & Toyota Research Institute): 'Robot-Powered Data Flywheel' research where robots deployed in the wild do useful work while collecting data to adapt foundation models.

rows.name: Legge Robotics
rows.description: Robotic World Model (ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab): code for a neural-network simulator used for robust policy optimization and offline model-based RL on real robots.

rows.name: UMA
rows.description: UMA: robotics startup building 'robots with experience'; no product details published yet.

rows.name: Seed GR-RL
rows.description: GR-RL (ByteDance Seed): RL framework that turns a generalist VLA policy into a specialist for long-horizon dexterous manipulation; first learning-based policy to lace a shoe autonomously (83.3% success).

rows.name: VLA SAFE
rows.description: SAFE (University of Toronto, Vector Institute & Toyota Research Institute, NeurIPS 2025): multitask failure detector for vision-language-action models that flags failures zero-shot on unseen tasks.

rows.name: Physical Intelligence
rows.description: Physical Intelligence (π): San Francisco company developing general robot foundation models (π0, π0.5, π0.7); π0 and π0.5 weights and code are open-sourced in openpi.

rows.name: ThinAct
rows.description: ThinkAct (NVIDIA & National Taiwan University, NeurIPS 2025): reasoning VLA framework that plans before acting via reinforced visual latent planning, enabling long-horizon planning and self-correction.

rows.name: TNKR
rows.description: Tnkr: IDE for physical agents (Tnkr Studio) to design, remix and deploy open robot designs run by any model, and sell them as kits.

rows.name: MicroAGI
rows.description: MicroAGI: data research lab working on end-to-end physical AGI, focused on reliable real-world robot deployments.

rows.name: Covariant
rows.description: Covariant: developer of RFM-1 (2024), an 8B-parameter robotics foundation model for warehouse picking. In Aug 2024 Amazon licensed its models and hired its founders.

rows.name: Sereact
rows.description: Sereact: company building a vision-language-action AI ('One Brain. Any Robot.') trained on large real-world robotic picking data for warehouse and logistics robots.

rows.name: Pantograph
rows.description: Pantograph: San Francisco public benefit research lab developing generally intelligent robots with simple, scalable methods; maker of the Pandroid robot.

rows.name: ProtoMotions
rows.description: ProtoMotions (NVIDIA): open-source (Apache-2.0) GPU-accelerated simulation and learning framework for training simulated digital humans and humanoid robots (e.g. Unitree G1/H1), with Newton, IsaacLab and MuJoCo backends.

rows.name: RoboArena
rows.description: RoboArena: community-run, distributed real-world benchmark that ranks generalist robot policies through double-blind pairwise evaluations on the DROID platform.

rows.name: Co-training
rows.description: Toyota Research Institute study on co-training Large Behavior Models (VLA) with heterogeneous data, using 4,000 h of robot and human data and 50M vision-language samples.

rows.name: General Intuition
rows.description: General Intuition: frontier lab building models that perceive, predict and act in virtual and physical environments (spatial-temporal agents).

rows.name: DreamZero
rows.description: DreamZero (NVIDIA): World Action Model built on a pretrained video diffusion backbone that jointly predicts future video and actions, generalizing over 2x better than VLAs to new tasks.

rows.name: Gigabrain
rows.description: GigaBrain-0.5M* (GigaAI): VLA model trained with world model-based reinforcement learning for robust cross-task adaptation and long-horizon manipulation.

rows.name: Xiaomi Robotics
rows.description: Xiaomi-Robotics-0 (Xiaomi): vision-language-action model optimized for fast, smooth real-time execution, pre-trained on cross-embodiment robot trajectories and vision-language data.

rows.name: Sureform
rows.description: Sureform: turns companies' internal operational data into RL environments and de-identified datasets licensed to AI labs for model training.

rows.name: OpenCastor
rows.description: OpenCastor: open-source runtime that connects AI models to robot bodies; a local model drafts a bounded plan from a spoken or typed instruction for the user to approve.

rows.name: Phys Mem
rows.description: PhysMem (Stanford & UC San Diego): test-time memory framework that lets VLM robot planners learn physical principles from interaction without updating model parameters.

rows.name: Memories
rows.description: Memories.ai: video data lake for physical AI offering egocentric data and dense annotation of customer video for robot training.

rows.name: Anvil
rows.description: Anvil Robotics: hardware and software platform with ready-to-run devkits (OpenARM, OpenYAM) to collect data, train and deploy physical AI policies.

rows.name: Mimic Video
rows.description: mimic-video (mimic robotics, ETH Zurich, Microsoft Zurich): Video-Action Model that grounds robot policies in pretrained video models instead of vision-language backbones.

rows.name: Mind Robotics
rows.description: Mind Robotics: builds foundation models and robots for industrial work, training on live production data with Rivian as first manufacturing partner.

rows.name: Latent
rows.description: LATENT (Tsinghua University, Galbot et al.): system that learns athletic humanoid tennis skills from imperfect human motion data.
other_descriptions: Learning Athletic Humanoid Tennis Skills from Imperfect Human Motion Data

rows.name: Simfoundry
rows.description: SimFoundry (NVIDIA & partners): automated real-to-sim system that turns a single image or video of a real scene into an interactive simulation for robot policy training and evaluation.

rows.name: Vision-Language-Delta-Action
rows.description: LoongForge-VLDA (Baidu & Harbin Institute of Technology Shenzhen): model architecture extending π0.5 with latent world modeling, learning compact 'Deltas' to guide robotic manipulation actions.

rows.name: Embo
rows.description: Embo: developing world-model-based AI for humanoid control, combining video/text pretraining, robot experience and reinforcement learning in imagined scenarios. Announced 23 Nov 2026; capabilities are company claims. No named model release, public API or weights identified in the reviewed announcement.

rows.name: Natura-1 (Nature Will)
rows.description: AI foundation model for the physical world; not an identified proprietary humanoid robot. Reclassified from Humanoids on 2026-11-23 using the existing record, last reviewed 2026-10-29; capabilities and availability not reverified.

rows.name: UnifoLM-WLA-1.0 (Unitree)
rows.description: One Model Driven, Whole-Body Coordination

rows.name: DreamDojo (NVIDIA)
rows.description: A Generalist Robot World Model from Large-Scale Human Videos

rows.name: Sonic (NVIDIA)
rows.description: Supersizing Motion Tracking for Natural Humanoid Whole-Body Control

rows.name: GR00T (NVIDIA)
rows.description: An Improved Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots

rows.name: Mjlab (NVIDIA)
rows.description: We took Isaac Lab’s proven manager-based architecture and RL abstractions, then built them directly on MuJoCo Warp. No translation layers, no Omniverse overhead. Just fast, transparent physics.

rows.name: GEAR-SONIC (NVIDIA)
rows.description: Supersizing Motion Tracking for Natural Humanoid Whole-Body Control

rows.name: CHIP (NVIDIA)
rows.description: Learning Adaptive Compliance for Humanoid Control through Hindsight Perturbation

rows.name: ResMimic (Amazon)
rows.description: A two-stage residual framework that unleashes the power of pre-trained general motion tracking policy

rows.name: VLK (Amazon)
rows.description: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from Synthetic Interactions in Reconstructed Scenes

rows.name: RynnBrain (Alibaba)
rows.description: An embodied foundation model grounded in physical reality. Moving beyond passive observation, RynnBrain anchors its understanding in the physical world through comprehensive egocentric cognition, precise spatiotemporal grounding, and real task planning

rows.name: VisualMimic
rows.description: Visual Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via Motion Tracking and Generation

rows.name: HDMI
rows.description: Learning Interactive Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Human Videos

rows.name: HITTER
rows.description: A HumanoId Table TEnnis Robot via Hierarchical Planning and Learning

rows.name: DreamControl
rows.description: Human-Inspired Whole-Body Humanoid Control for Scene Interaction via Guided Diffusion

rows.name: PhysHSI
rows.description: Towards a Real-World Generalizable and Natural Humanoid-Scene Interaction System

rows.name: SoftMimic
rows.description: Learning Compliant Whole-body Control from Examples

rows.name: Goalkeeper
rows.description: Learning from Position Conditioned Task-Motion Constraints

rows.name: BFM-Zero
rows.description: A Promptable Behavioral Foundation Model for Humanoid Control Using Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning

rows.name: GentleHumanoid
rows.description: Learning Upper-body Compliance for Contact-rich Human and Object Interaction

rows.name: Amo
rows.description: Adaptive Motion Optimization for Hyper-Dexterous Humanoid Whole-Body Control

rows.name: Viral
rows.description: Visual Sim-to-Real at Scale for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

rows.name: Gallant
rows.description: Voxel Grid-based Humanoid Locomotion and Local-navigation across 3D Constrained Terrains

rows.name: OmniRetarget
rows.description: Interaction-Preserving Data Generation for Humanoid Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation and Scene Interaction

rows.name: BeyondMimic
rows.description: From Motion Tracking to Versatile Humanoid Control via Guided Diffusion

rows.name: Holosoma
rows.description: A comprehensive humanoid robotics framework for training and deploying reinforcement learning policies on humanoid robots, as well as motion retargeting

rows.name: DoorMan
rows.description: Opening the Sim-to-Real Door for Humanoid Pixel-to-Action Policy Transfer

rows.name: Genmimic
rows.description: From Generated Human Videos to Physically Plausible Robot Trajectories

rows.name: Everyday
rows.description: A Comprehensive Robotic Dataset for Open-World Humanoid Manipulation

rows.name: Extreme control
rows.description: Low-Latency Humanoid Teleoperation with Direct Extremity Control

rows.name: Humi
rows.description: Humanoid Manipulation Interface: Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation from Robot-Free Demonstrations

rows.name: Halo
rows.description: Learning Human-Robot Collaboration via Heterogeneous-Agent Lyapunov Policy Optimization

rows.name: Ladderman
rows.description: Learning Humanoid Perceptive Ladder Climbing

rows.name: Halo (Apple)
rows.description: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation

rows.name: Reflex
rows.description: Visually Grounded Reactive Humanoid Control

rows.name: Bambot
rows.description: BamBot: open-source project with browser-based simulations to play with and assemble low-cost robots (SO-ARM100, BamBot) and Unitree Go2/G1.

rows.name: Reachy
rows.description: Official Pollen Robotics Docker image with a standalone Reachy 2 core, for demos, testing and development without the physical robot.

rows.name: Gazebo
rows.description: Gazebo: open-source robot simulator (Open Robotics) to iterate on designs and control strategies, widely used with ROS.

rows.name: Robotics Pick and Place
rows.description: Google AI Studio demo app: a Franka arm simulated in the browser with MuJoCo, where Gemini Robotics-ER detects objects and performs pick-and-place from text prompts.

rows.name: NVIDIA Newton
rows.description: NVIDIA Newton: open-source, GPU-accelerated physics engine built on NVIDIA Warp for robotics simulation and research.

rows.name: Agibot
rows.description: AgiBot LinkCraft: AgiBot platform to choreograph robot motions, audio and expressions with 3D scene preview and a timeline editor, generating content the robot can execute.

rows.name: ABB RobotStudio
rows.description: ABB RobotStudio: ABB's offline programming and simulation software to model, program and test robot cells in 3D, using the same virtual controller software as real ABB robots.

rows.name: Blueprint
rows.description: Blueprint: AI hardware design tool that turns a prompt into a buildable hardware project with wiring diagrams, bills of materials and assembly guides.

rows.name: Matlab Simulink
rows.description: MATLAB Simulink (MathWorks): block-diagram environment for model-based design and simulation of dynamic systems, used for robot control design and code generation.

rows.name: Articraft
rows.description: Articraft: agentic system where a coding agent generates simulation-ready articulated 3D assets from text descriptions.

rows.name: Lelab
rows.description: LeLab (Hugging Face): browser-based GUI for LeRobot covering calibration, teleoperation, dataset recording, training and inference.

rows.name: Lucky Robots
rows.description: Lucky Engine (Lucky Robots): local robot simulation app combining MuJoCo physics with a visual editor; free for research and personal use.

rows.name: FLUX-mimic (mimic robotics)
rows.description: Video-action model trained on top of Black Forest Labs' FLUX 3 for data-efficient dexterous industrial manipulation

rows.name: Viam
rows.description: Viam: robot software platform presented as a harness for AI agents to develop, deploy and operate robot applications on mixed hardware; the open-source viam-server runs on the robot and enforces limits, and outside agents connect through the Viam MCP server.

rows.name: WALL-OSS-1.0 (X Square Robot)
rows.description: X Square Robot's vision-language-action foundation model (2026-11-23), built from a Qwen3.5 base, with Lite (4B) and Nano (2B) variants; the company reports 55.1% zero-shot success across 312 evaluator-chosen tasks on physical robots. Licence and model weights are not stated in the announcement.

rows.name: AHEADance
rows.description: Anticipatory Humanoid Dance from Streaming Audio (UCL Humanoid Robotics Lab): generates targets for a Unitree G1's 29 joints 30 times a second from live audio, shown on the real robot with eight songs in seven styles (arXiv 2611.13370; code announced, not yet released).

rows.name: Play2Perfect
rows.description: What Matters in Dexterous Play Pretraining for Precise Assembly? Two-stage reinforcement learning: free play with diverse objects in simulation, then fine-tuning for contact-rich precise assembly with multi-fingered hands, transferred zero-shot to real hardware (CoRL 2026; arXiv 2606.26428; code on GitHub).
